levels.prefix: The following is general background on retail inventory management practices. Inventory management is a critical function in retail operations, balancing the cost of holding stock against the risk of stockouts. Economic order quantity models help determine optimal reorder points and batch sizes. Safety stock calculations account for demand variability and supplier lead time uncertainty. ABC analysis categorises inventory by value and turnover velocity, allowing differentiated management policies. Just-in-time inventory strategies minimise holding costs but increase vulnerability to supply disruptions. Perpetual inventory systems track stock levels in real time, while periodic systems conduct batch counts at fixed intervals. Shrinkage — loss from theft, damage, or administrative error — typically accounts for 1-2% of retail inventory value annually.
